summary: Taj Mahal is a tense, cutthroat auction game where you bid cards across twelve rounds to win majorities in one of five categories, then cash those wins into palaces and commodities for points; it plays fast and mean, with players baiting each other into overspending or ganging up to deny a leader.
praised: Tight, tense bidding mechanism where knowing when to drop out is the whole game
Constant player interaction and 'kingmaking' tension without direct conflict
Short, brisk playtime relative to the depth of decisions
Elegant, tightly designed Knizia ruleset with little downtime
criticised: Heavy multiplayer solitaire risk if players don't actively gang up on the leader
Can feel mean or swingy — a coalition can crush a leading player
Thin theme bolted onto an abstract bidding system
Component/board iconography can be fiddly to learn at first

interaction.kind: auction bluffing and coalition-building to deny the leader

scoring.why: the winner is decided by who best times card commitments across the palace/commodity auctions to bank the most cumulative influence points
